_comment: Config keys this project has REMOVED, mapped to their replacement. Powers the PRD-QUAL-131-FR04 warning: TRWConfig is extra="ignore", so a removed key is dropped in silence and the operator who tuned it never learns it is gone. An empty replacement means there is none -- most of these knobs were never wired to anything, so there is nothing to point at, and saying so is more useful than saying nothing. Add an entry in the same commit that removes a field, and name it in the CHANGELOG Removed section.

retired.dispatch_role_client: dispatch_default_client (or pass --client); a role no longer picks the client

_comment_owned_elsewhere: Keys that live in .trw/config.yaml but are owned by a subsystem OTHER than TRWConfig, mapped to their owner. They are legitimate and must NOT be warned about: the warning compares against TRWConfig's field set, which is not the whole of what the file legitimately holds. Warning on a working key trains an operator to ignore the warning, which costs more than the silence it was built to fix. Add an entry when a subsystem starts reading or writing its own key here, and name the read site so the claim is checkable. The SHELL-HOOK entries below are derived, not trusted: tests/test_config_owned_key_derivation.py rescans the bundled hooks and fails if any config.yaml key they read is absent from this map, so a new hook knob cannot ship as a false 'typo' warning.

owned_elsewhere.cc03_hook_enabled: bundled shell hooks (top-level CC-03 enable override, read at claude_code/hooks/lib-distill-hint.sh:122, copilot/hooks/lib-copilot-distill-hint.sh:127, hooks/cursor/lib-distill-hint.sh — THE canonical key, and the highest-priority one, ahead of both channels.* spellings; the same hooks also accept channels.cc03_hook_enabled/channels.cc03.enabled, exempted via the 'channels' entry below)
owned_elsewhere.claude_code_statusline: trw_mcp.bootstrap._settings_merge.statusline_enabled (top-level opt-out for the Claude Code statusLine entry; false removes a TRW-owned statusLine on init/update, PRD-CORE-354 FR06)
owned_elsewhere.channels: bundled shell hooks + trw_mcp.channels.claude_code._hook_helpers.read_cc03_config (nested block; the only key read there today is cc03_hook_enabled/cc03.enabled, an ACCEPTED alternate spelling of the canonical top-level cc03_hook_enabled above -- release-window fix, 2026-09-27, closing the 'has no effect' false warning on channels: {cc03_hook_enabled: true})
owned_elsewhere.memory_hot_max_entries: trw_memory.models._config_sources (the yaml source maps it onto MemoryConfig.hot_max_entries); trw-mcp no longer declares or reads it
owned_elsewhere.memory_score_w1: trw_memory.models._config_sources (maps onto MemoryConfig.score_relevance_weight); trw-mcp no longer declares or reads it
owned_elsewhere.memory_score_w2: trw_memory.models._config_sources (maps onto MemoryConfig.score_recency_weight); trw-mcp no longer declares or reads it
owned_elsewhere.memory_score_w3: trw_memory.models._config_sources (maps onto MemoryConfig.score_importance_weight); trw-mcp no longer declares or reads it
owned_elsewhere.platform_org_name: trw_mcp.cli.auth (written at auth.py:351, read back at auth.py:300 to render auth status)
owned_elsewhere.platform_user_email: trw_mcp.cli.auth (written at auth.py:353, read back at auth.py:302 to render auth status)
owned_elsewhere.sqlite_vec_enabled: install-trw.py optional-features memo written by installers before trw-mcp 6.1.0. sqlite-vec is a base dependency since 6.1.0, so the installer neither writes nor reads it; kept here so configs from older installs are not warned about
owned_elsewhere.stop_deliver_window_minutes: bundled shell hooks (documented project-level override for the PRD-FIX-117/118 stop-deliver reminder window, read at hooks/lib-trw.sh:317)
